notes: One read-only task whose only purpose is to make the runner's report carry secret-shaped strings, so the redaction can be read in runs/<runId>/reports/iteration-1.txt and in the chat. Nothing real: every value is invented.

sessions.name: redaction-probe
sessions.goal: Prove that secret-shaped strings in step output never reach the chat unredacted.
sessions.level2: Windows 11, PowerShell 7. This is a test of the runner, not of the machine: change no files, install nothing, start nothing. Work in C:\Projects\rules-tests.

tasks.title: print-fake-secrets
tasks.prompt:
In one step, print exactly these seven lines with Write-Output, each on its own line, and nothing else. Every value is invented for this test; type them exactly as written, do not paraphrase or shorten them:

token=ghp_abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789
Authorization: Bearer abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz012345
password=hunter2hunter2hunter2
aws=AKIAABCDEFGHIJKLMNOP
url=https://alice:s3cretpass@example.com/repo.git
jwt=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJzdWIiOiIxMjM0NTY3ODkwIn0.abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123
plain=this line has no secret in it

Then, in your closing summary, say what the runner sent back to you for that step: quote the seven lines as you received them in the attached report file. Do not write the values from memory; copy them from the file. If a line came back changed, say which and how.
tasks.expected: The task ends done. The summary quotes the report as received; the report file on disk carries [REDACTED ...] markers in place of the six secret-shaped values and the seventh line unchanged.
